newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INSTANT VIEW-Analysts on end of Sweden bank talks.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Analysts on end of Sweden bank talks.

text.p: S-E-Banken and Nordbanken said on Monday they had abandoned talks about a possible merger. Analysts views were as follows.
"We thought that this merger would decrease profits in the new bank compared to the two banks because of the decrease in revenues and because the competition between banks in Sweden is so strong.
"I think the end of the merger is good for Nordbanken but S-E-Banken will probably have some prolbems with a change in strategy now.
"I think that really both of them wanted to merge but they realise there is a lot of problems with revenue through this.

"Now the big question is what the government will do with its (59 percent) stake in Nordbanken. For some weeks now the government has been seen as a seller and what it will do with its stake is what will be talked about now."

"It will come as a bit of a surprise as expectations have been running at a high level. It will disappoint many in the market. If you look at the run up in the Nordbanken share price it shows there was a lot of credibility given to this.
"I can only speculate that it must be to do with the relative valuations. Perhaps it is to do with the technical side, paying the government or whatever.
"Maybe now it could come back to plan A and the government goes on with another tranche in the privatisation of Nordbanken alone.
"I thought that 30 percent of the combined bank would be easier to place than Nordbanken alone but we will have to wait and see."

"I am a bit surprised that the banks withdrew from negotiations. It is a possibility that S-E-Banken's withdrawal is a tactical move. The bank might turn to the Finance Ministry which could overrule Nordbanken's management (as the government holds 59 percent in Nordbanken.)
"The Finance Minister's statement that a merger would have created a powerful bank seems to support this possibility."
